$meta.name: VendorTradeType
$meta.description: The trade a vendor practises. Stored as free text in `providers.type` and `tasks.category`, and read by the CAPEX/OPEX classification engine.
$meta.ownerNote: OWNERSHIP IS INVERTED here and that is the whole point of shipping it. The trade list is client-owned: an installed mobile binary cannot be recalled and already writes the prefixed localization key on every vendor edit, so the canonical spelling is whatever mobile sends — not whatever the server would have preferred. These values are seeded FROM mobile's ServiceProviderType, and the server's job is to spell a known trade consistently, never to police which trades exist.
$meta.onUnknownNote: COERCE, NEVER REJECT. A trade absent from `values` is legitimate — it is stored verbatim. Rejecting would break a client that shipped a trade we have not heard of yet.
$meta.aliasMatchNote: The server normalizes by stripping a leading `serviceProvider` (any case) and lowercasing, then looking the remainder up (babel-lambda-api/src/service/capex-recommendation/capex-recommendation.types.ts:192-207, canonicalCategoryKey). Because every bare spelling of a KNOWN trade is listed explicitly below, a case-insensitive lookup over values + aliases reproduces that behaviour exactly. The prefix strip only ever mattered for an UNKNOWN trade, and an unknown trade is preserved verbatim anyway.

provenance.seededFrom: babel-mobile/lib/models/babel_localized_enums.dart:127-163 — `enum ServiceProviderType with LocalizedEnum`. `values` are the enum KEYS; `aliases` are the enum MEMBER NAMES (`.name`), which is the bare spelling that leaked to production.

drift.note: Uniquely, the three code-level lists AGREE — 23/23/23, same order. The drift is in the DATA and in the label catalogues, and it has already cost a live defect.
drift.storedData: TWO spellings reached production for the same trades: the localization key (`serviceProviderPlumbing`) and the bare enum member (`plumbing`), the latter being `.name` serialized where `.key` was meant.
drift.shippedDefect: The CAPEX/OPEX engine keys its rule table on the localization key and matched with `===`, so bare-typed vendors scored nothing and the engine silently returned NO suggestion for most vendors. api#1153 fixed the matching; trade-vocabulary.ts fixed the spelling on write. This contract is what stops a third client re-introducing it.
drift.labelCatalogue: babel-admin-panel/src/i18n/*.json carries 25 `serviceProvider*` keys — two orphans, `serviceProviderInspector` and `serviceProviderManagement`, have no counterpart in ANY repo's code. Mobile has exactly 23. Left out of `values` deliberately: adding a trade because a translator typed a label is backwards.

aliasesNote: Legacy bare spellings still present in stored rows. Readers must accept them and MAP THEM to the canonical value; writers must emit only `values`. A caller matching the RAW column in SQL needs both spellings — see trade-vocabulary.ts storedSpellingsOf.
